answer: Each collapsed cluster gets one timber weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. The ember report makes public the merge explicitly at each lantern. Because of that, an hostile operator who spins up 107 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 217 times the capital for one share. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 40 times over for the same share of the pool. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
